title: At the mouth of the Duero the Castilian admiral Pedro, with 14 ships, attacks the joined fleets of Catalonia and Fās, 124 sail under the Marīnid prince Khālid. He is driven off without losing a ship, but the allies lose 29, most of them transports, and two are taken

commanders.allies: Khālid, a Marīnid prince, a naval showman (37/60/72)

data.note: the battle is counted a win for the allies; the allied losses include 23 transports, 2 of them captured

source: autosave of 1 March 1411 (the war's battle list)

title: The Emperor's first great battle. On 17 Ramaḍān, the day of Badr, the Emperor Ismāʿīl with 25,730 men, Andalusīs and Marīnids, attacks Crisanto's 19,290 at Cuéllar, where the Catalans had been broken a month before. It is a hard day: 9,590 of ours fall for 8,450 of theirs, but the field is ours
source: Trent's battle screen, 13 January 1411; autosave of 1 March 1411

title: At Coimbra 940 Marīnids attack the Portuguese army of 13,440 and are destroyed
source: autosave of 1 March 1411 (the war's battle list)

title: At Ledesma the Emperor's army of 14,500 catches the 320 men of Castile's heir, Prince Fernando, and kills 130; the prince escapes
source: save of 1 November 1411, before the peace (the war's battle list)

title: The great sea battle off al-Ushbūna. In the bay of Setúbal the Castilian admiral Pedro, with 14 ships, attacks the joined fleets of al-Andalus and Fās, 107 sail under the Marīnid prince Aḥmad, and loses every ship; the allies lose 12

data.location: the bay of Setúbal, south of al-Ushbūna

commanders.allies: Aḥmad, a Marīnid prince, a naval showman and battlefield medic (57/50/56)

data.note: Trent's major sea battle off the shores of Lisbon

source: save of 1 November 1411, before the peace (the war's battle list)

title: On the outskirts of Zamora the Emperor meets Crisanto's host again at Toro, 20,890 against 11,110, and breaks it: 5,120 Castilians lost for 4,280 of ours
source: Trent's battle screen, 15 May 1411

title: Off Cape Mondego the three Catalan ships of Berenguer Ramon, ruler of Catalonia, attack the Portuguese fleet of 17 and lose two
source: save of 1 November 1411, before the peace (the war's battle list)

title: At Coimbra the Portuguese army, 13,380 under Ponce, attacks 5,850 Marīnids under Ṭālib and is thrown back: 4,510 Portuguese lost for 2,560

commanders.Morocco: Ṭālib, an Andalusī, born to the saddle

source: save of 1 November 1411, before the peace (the war's battle list)

title: The crown prince's first sea battle. At the mouth of the Duero the Portuguese fleet of 17 attacks 34 ships, 23 of al-Andalus under the crown prince Muḥammad and 11 of Valencia under their own admiral, and loses 15 of them for 3 of ours

commanders.al-Andalus: the crown prince Muḥammad, in his first sea battle (Trent)
commanders.Valencia: Otto, the Valencian admiral, an aggressive commander (76/62/43), whom the save lists as commander of the allied side

source: Trent's battle screen (breakdown) and account, 21 June 1411; save of 1 November 1411

title: At Moncorvo the Marīnid prince Fāris, son of the sultan of Fās, with 3,000 attacks Crisanto's 6,380 and is beaten off; each side loses about 600

commanders.Morocco: Fāris, son of Abū al-Faḍl of Fās, a hardy warrior

source: save of 1 November 1411, before the peace (the war's battle list)

title: At Besteiros, between Viseu and Coimbra, the Emperor with 11,370 destroys more than half the Portuguese army of 9,670: 5,280 of theirs lost for 1,920 of ours
source: save of 1 November 1411, before the peace (the war's battle list)

title: Qashtāla surrenders unconditionally. Its armies gone and its lands occupied from Zamora to Galicia, the Crown of Castile capitulates to the Emperor, who may now dictate the terms of peace. War score stands at 100

data.event: Capitulation! (the game's notice: Castile has unconditionally surrendered in the Reconquest of Iberia; we control their lands and may dictate the terms of peace)
data.armiesOnScreen: our armies of 3,035, 5,588, 1,809, 2,169, 1,303 and 1,399 across León and Galicia, with Santiago de Compostela, Ponferrada and Zamora flying the Emperor's flag; the main army 9,437

source: Trent's screen, 2 September 1411

title: With Qashtāla at his mercy, the Emperor turns on Portugal and marches on Porto, its capital, while the crown prince Muḥammad brings the fleet round to blockade the city from the sea. Portugal has not surrendered. A separate peace with it is possible, but the Emperor wants no concessions from Portugal: this war is to be the end of it

data.warAim: no separate peace for concessions; the end of Portugal as a kingdom (Trent)

source: Trent's account, September 1411

title: Off Cape São Vicente the Marīnid fleet, 14 sail under Prince Khālid, catches the last three Castilian ships under Pedro and sinks two
source: save of 1 November 1411, before the peace (the war's battle list)

title: Porto falls. Starved by the Emperor's siege on land and the crown prince's blockade at sea, its people rise and throw open the gates to the army. So ends the Kingdom of Portugal

data.how: the city was starving; a revolt of the populace opened the gates (Trent)

source: Trent's account, 7 October 1411

title: The last battle. Three weeks after Porto fell, the last Portuguese army, 4,800 under Bernardo, marches on a force of Marīnid levies; the Emperor intercepts it at Guimarães, the cradle of the kingdom, with 9,450 men and kills or scatters 3,160 for the loss of 1,150

data.side: al-Andalus attacking: the Emperor intercepted the Portuguese as they moved against a Marīnid force of levies (Trent)

commanders.Portugal: Bernardo, an ironside and defensive planner (83/84/56)

source: Trent's battle screen, 27 October 1411; save of 1 November 1411

title: The Peace of Rajab (14 Rajab 814). Portugal ceases to be: all 34 of its towns, from Porto, Braga and Guimarães to Coimbra, Viseu and Bragança, pass to the crown. Qashtāla gives up 63 towns, the heart of Old Castile, León and Navarre: Valladolid, Burgos, León, Zamora, Toro, Palencia, Segovia, Soria and Logroño, and Pamplona, Tudela and Estella. What is left of Qashtāla, 45 towns in Galicia, Asturias, Cantabria and the Basque country, is ruled from Oviedo

title: The conquests of Jillīqiya are given out as four new ṭāʾifas. The Emperor's cousin Aḥmad takes the old Kingdom of Portugal as the Ṭāʾifa of Burtuqāl; the Emperor's son Aḥmad, eighteen, takes León; Khālid ibn Yaḥyā Raḥḥū, sixty-eight, takes Old Castile as the Ṭāʾifa of Burghush; and the Emperor's cousin Yūsuf takes Navarre as the Ṭāʾifa of Banbalūna. The crown keeps its 161 towns

taifas.Burtuqāl (ABA10), seat Barcelos: 34 towns, 675,000 people, Portuguese; Aḥmad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Yūsuf, 34 (58/41/72)
taifas.Liyūn (ABA42), seat León: 17 towns, 387,000 people, Leonese; Aḥmad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd, the Emperor's son, 18 (47/64/35)
taifas.Burghush (ABA49), seat Burgos: 28 towns, 584,000 people, Castilian; Khālid ibn Yaḥyā Raḥḥū, 68 (81/85/78), heir Abū Ḥammū
taifas.Banbalūna (ABA55), seat Pamplona: 18 towns, 271,000 people, Basque; Yūsuf ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Yūsuf, 39 (56/30/63)

source: save of 1 November 1411, after the organisation of the conquests (Trent)

title: Europe is horrified by the conquest of Portugal and Old Castile, all but Paris. The Holy Roman Emperor can do little about it, with France and England at war again

title: Four weeks after the Peace of Rajab the Ḥafṣids of Tūnis enter an alliance with al-Andalus. With Fās and Miṣr, the empire is now allied to every great Muslim power of the Maghrib and to the Mamlūks
source: save of 11 August 1420 (the treaty list; the snapshots of 1414 and 1416 were corrected)
